hero.lead: A copper nation of 21.9 million that restructured $3 billion of bonds in 2024, and where four in ten citizens are undernourished.

stats.label: Natural resource rents, share of GDP

capital.heading: 25 instruments. A restructured debt, a bond swapped for power, and World Bank, AfDB, US and EU finance for food, schools, water and the Lobito corridor.

record.text: 2053 Eurobond bought back in June 2026 with a $600 million African Development Bank Group loan and the Government’s own resources; $275 million earmarked for the energy sector
New 36-month Extended Credit Facility agreed with IMF staff on 9 October 2026 (SDR 1,076 million), subject to Executive Board approval and agreed prior actions
Eurobonds restructured in 2024: the notes due 2022, 2024 and 2027, of $750 million, $1 billion and $1.25 billion, approved by holders of more than 94% of the outstanding principal of each series
IMF Extended Credit Facility completed on 27 January 2026: SDR 1,271.66 million disbursed in all, after an augmentation in June 2024
Public debt as a share of GDP in 2024 (IMF estimate), down from 133.4% in 2023; the IMF projects 87.6% for 2025

register.name: Buyback of the 2053 Eurobond, a debt-for-development swap for the grid
register.detail: Tender offer announcement of 4 June 2026 for $1,364,725,564 of Fixed Rate Step-Up Amortising Notes due 2053 · $740 per $1,000 plus early fees · Financed with a $600 million African Development Bank Group loan and the Government’s own resources
register.note: $275 million earmarked for investment in the energy sector
register.text: Zambia bought back its $1.36 billion 2053 Eurobond, one of the two bonds issued in the 2024 restructuring, with a $600 million loan from the African Development Bank Group and its own resources. The Government has committed to earmark $275 million, to be invested in the energy sector to provide reliable and affordable electricity. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Eurobond restructuring
register.detail: Agreement in principle 25 March 2024 · Approved by holders of 97.23% of the 2022 notes, 94.06% of the 2024 notes and 97.42% of the 2027 notes · Exchange implemented 11 June 2024
register.note: Exchanged for new bonds of $1.72 billion due 2033 and $1.36 billion due 2053
register.text: The exchange of Zambia’s three Eurobonds, of $750 million due 2022, $1 billion due 2024 and $1.25 billion due 2027, for two new amortising bonds. The IMF records the exchange as implemented on 11 June 2024, with significant external debt service relief that protects the budget for the seven standards.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility, new arrangement
register.detail: Staff-level agreement 9 October 2026 · SDR 1,076 million · 36 months · Subject to IMF Executive Board approval and agreed prior actions
register.note: Inflation 6.1% and gross international reserves $6.1 billion in September 2026
register.text: A proposed new IMF arrangement of $1,472 million over 36 months, to support macroeconomic stability, debt sustainability, rebuilt buffers and private-sector-led growth. It follows the arrangement completed in January 2026 and anchors the public finances behind the seven standards.

register.name: Zambia–Malawi Interconnector Project
register.detail: Announced 23 July 2026 · IDA grant · Part of the RETRADE-SA Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach · About 47 km in Zambia of the 192 km, 400 kV corridor
register.note: Access to regional electricity markets for Zambia and Malawi
register.text: Finances the Zambian section of a 400 kV transmission line to Malawi, about 47 km of a 192 km corridor. It gives both countries access to regional electricity markets, a more diverse supply and greater resilience to climate shocks, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Catalyzing a Climate Risk Protection Shield for Zambian Smallholder Farmers (SAP067)
register.detail: Approved by the GCF Board 28 March 2026 (B.44) · Grant · Entity: Ministry of Finance and National Planning · Estimated completion 28 March 2031
register.note: Total value $30.3 million; 840,000 people in smallholder households
register.text: Green Climate Fund grant to build the climate resilience of 840,000 people in Zambian smallholder households, with improved insurance products expected to reach 140,000 farming households and agroforestry packages 65,000 households. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Second Zambia Climate and Economic Resilience Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved, announced 16 March 2026 · Grant · Second operation of a programmatic series
register.note: Follows the first operation, of $100 million
register.text: Budget support for reforms in fiscal management and resilience, mineral revenue transparency, state-owned enterprise governance, carbon markets, public-private partnerships, renewable energy, disaster risk management, adaptive social protection and the financial sustainability of the water sector. It protects the livelihood, energy and water standards against shocks.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved 31 August 2022 for SDR 978.2 million, 100 percent of quota · Augmented 26 June 2024 to SDR 1,271.66 million, 130 percent of quota · Sixth and final review completed 27 January 2026
register.note: SDR 1,271.66 million disbursed in all; the last SDR 138.9 million (about $190 million) in January 2026
register.text: IMF lending that supported Zambia’s economic programme through its debt restructuring, augmented in June 2024, when a severe drought had hit agriculture and electricity generation. With the final review the full SDR 1,271.66 million, about $1.7 billion, had been disbursed.

register.name: Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development, second phase (TRALARD II)
register.detail: Approved, announced 24 September 2025 · IDA grant · $37 million more in grants from the GEF, the LDCF, the Africa Climate and People Trust Fund (funded by the NDF), the SCF and SCALE
register.note: Total investment $137 million; over 650,000 people
register.text: Sustainable land management over more than 680,000 hectares of the Miombo ecoregion: climate-smart agriculture, restoration of degraded landscapes, hydromet services and community forest management, with a new jurisdictional emission reduction programme for carbon markets. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (DZAP)
register.detail: Approved, announced 23 September 2025 · IDA grant
register.note: Broadband, digital public platforms and digital skills
register.text: Extends backbone and last-mile broadband, builds interoperable and secure platforms for digital government services and regional trade, and develops employment-ready digital skills among young people and underserved groups. It serves the livelihood and education standards.

register.name: Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation (ASCENT Zambia)
register.detail: Approved, announced 28 July 2025 · IDA grant · 13th phase of the regional ASCENT programme
register.note: More than one million beneficiaries within five years
register.text: Electricity for remote and underserved communities and reliable power for businesses, with new technologies and local capacity to maintain energy infrastructure. It serves the energy standard and is part of Mission 300, the goal of reaching 300 million people in Africa by 2030.

register.name: Water Supply and Sanitation Services in Growth Centers Program
register.detail: Approved, announced 28 April 2025 · IDA grant
register.note: Kafubu, Luapula, North-western and Western water utilities
register.text: Supports sector governance reforms, better billing, lower water losses and more household water connections and latrines, reaching growth centres and rural areas. It serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: First Climate and Economic Resilience Development Policy Financing with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.detail: Approved, announced 18 December 2024 · IDA grant · $25 million development policy financing and $75 million Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option
register.note: Quick liquidity after a national disaster
register.text: Budget support for Zambia’s resilience to natural disasters and other shocks, which also helps to cover budget pressures from the drought, with $75 million of contingent financing that provides quick liquidity after a national disaster. It protects the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Scaling-up Shock Responsive Social Protection, Second Additional Financing
register.detail: Announced 9 July 2024 · IDA grant from the Crisis Response Window · Emergency cash assistance over 12 months
register.note: Will include a $7.6 million grant from the GEWEL multi-donor trust fund
register.text: Emergency cash assistance through the Social Cash Transfer programme in 84 drought-affected districts, for about 904,635 current beneficiary households and over 726,361 new drought-affected households. It serves the food standard.

register.name: Girls’ Education and Women’s Empowerment and Livelihoods for Human Capital (GEWEL 2)
register.detail: Announced 28 March 2024 · IDA grant E3020-ZM, SDR 112.8 million · Financing Agreement signed 30 April 2024 · $150 million IDA and $7 million Global Financing Facility · Closing 30 June 2028
register.note: More than 107,000 adolescent girls kept in school
register.text: Keeps more than 107,000 vulnerable adolescent girls in school, widens economic opportunities for 58,000 women, strengthens adaptive social protection and supports nutrition for at least 25,000 households in the hardest-to-reach communities. It serves the education standard, which sets Zambia’s Coverage, and the livelihood standard.

register.name: Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER)
register.detail: Announced 20 February 2024 · IDA grant E2930-ZM, SDR 201.2 million · Financing Agreement signed 7 March 2024 · Closing 27 February 2030
register.note: 2.5 million people in Zambia, about 13% of the population
register.text: Rehabilitates the Serenje–Mpika section of the corridor to Tanzania, builds a One Stop Border Post at Nakonde and makes the corridor a SMART corridor with real-time traffic management. It serves the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Zambia Agribusiness and Trade Project II
register.detail: IDA credit 7345-ZM · Financing Agreement signed 12 December 2023 · Closing 15 December 2028
register.note: Markets, finance and firm growth in agribusiness
register.text: Aims to increase access to markets and finance and to promote firm growth in Zambia’s agribusiness sector. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Zambia Growth Opportunities Program
register.detail: Program Appraisal Document of 3 June 2022 · IDA credit · Program-for-Results · Closing 31 December 2026
register.note: Agricultural diversification and jobs in the agri-food sector
register.text: Results-based financing to promote agricultural diversification, sustainability and jobs in Zambia’s agri-food sector. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Lobito Economic Corridor, first tranche
register.detail: Approved, announced 6 August 2026 · African Development Fund loan, first tranche under ADF-16 · $10 million grant from the Rome Process/Mattei Plan Financing Facility · Financing may reach up to $500 million in later phases, subject to further resources
register.note: Some 550 km of railway in Zambia and 105 km of the Mwinilunga–Jimbe road
register.text: Concessional finance for the integrated Lobito economic corridor, which links Zambia to the Angolan port of Lobito. The project includes some 550 km of railway to be built in Zambia, the upgrade of 105 km of the Mwinilunga–Jimbe road, trade facilitation and institutional support, and the AfDB expects about 500 permanent and 5,000 temporary jobs. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Fiscal Sustainability and Economic Resilience Support Programme
register.detail: Approved, announced 12 December 2024 · Loan
register.note: Revenue, public investment and agricultural mechanisation
register.text: Supports reforms for fiscal sustainability and private sector participation, domestic revenue, including a smart invoice system and the registration of 12,000 VAT taxpayers, public investment management and agricultural mechanisation through ten mechanisation centres. It serves the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Zambia–EU Partnership for Education Reforms
register.detail: Signed 12 November 2025, EU–Zambia Lobito Corridor Business Forum, Lusaka · ZMW 1.05 billion · Led by the Government of Zambia
register.note: Access to secondary education and learning outcomes
register.text: European Union support for the Government of Zambia’s education reforms, focused on access to secondary education and on learning outcomes. It serves the education standard, which sets Zambia’s Coverage.

register.name: Railway Sector Support Programme
register.detail: Signed 12 November 2025 · EU contribution to a €117.5 million programme · Co-financed by the Government of Zambia, the private sector and the World Bank
register.note: Operability and efficiency of Zambia Railways Limited
register.text: European Union support to enhance the operability and efficiency of Zambia Railways Limited and to strengthen rail sector regulation, as the railways prepare for the Lobito corridor. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Nexus Energy Water in the Zambian Provinces Served by the Lobito Corridor (NEWZA 2.0)
register.detail: Signed 12 November 2025 · EU €20 million and Germany (BMZ) €21 million · ZMW 1.08 billion
register.note: Water supply through solar energy in North-Western and Copperbelt provinces
register.text: Team Europe finance to improve water supply through solar energy and efficiency in the North-Western and Copperbelt provinces. It serves the water and energy standards.

register.name: Zambia Compact II
register.detail: Signed 17 October 2024 · Millennium Challenge Corporation grant · Roads and Access, Asset Finance, Agriculture Policy Reform and the American Catalyst Facility for Development
register.note: With $33 million from Zambia, a $491 million compact
register.text: A United States grant compact to advance Zambia’s agriculture sector: 210 miles of road and transport infrastructure, investment in electricity, irrigation, logistics and processing equipment, and grain market policy reform. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Green African Agri Value Chain, ZICB Zambia
register.detail: Credit line signed 30 July 2025 · €4 million risk-sharing facility signed 10 November 2025, supported by a European Commission grant · ZICB to match the €15 million
register.note: €30 million in all for agri-food SMEs; at least 30% for women-led or women-owned businesses
register.text: EIB Global lending through Zambia Industrial Commercial Bank to small and medium-sized enterprises in agriculture value chains, with a risk-sharing facility that helps the bank lend to smaller agri-food firms and smallholder farmers. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Garneton North 20 MW Solar Project
register.detail: Approved, announced 31 October 2025 · AfDB $7.27 million from its own resources, matched by concessional finance from a development finance institution · GET FiT Zambia · 25-year power purchase agreement with ZESCO
register.note: Electricity for 82,000 people
register.text: A 20 MW solar plant in the Copperbelt Province with a 10 km, 33 kV line to the national grid, whose whole output ZESCO is to buy. The AfDB expects it to supply electricity to 82,000 people and avoid 58,740 tonnes of CO2 a year. It serves the energy standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Copper
items.label: Natural resource rents, share of GDP, 2021
items.text: The Copperbelt, linked to the Indian Ocean by rail and road, with some 550 km of new railway planned in Zambia to reach the Atlantic port of Lobito.
items.alt: A copper mine on the Zambian Copperbelt

items.name: The Rivers
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: The Zambezi and the Kafue: clean power, and 3,980 m³ of fresh water per person.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: Woodland across three-fifths of the country.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Room to grow more food, while 41% of people are undernourished.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Nearly half live in towns and cities.

items.name: Zambeef Products Plc
items.text: An integrated agribusiness running from crop production to animal feed, grain to flour and livestock to processed meat, with 236 retail outlets. In May 2025 the African Development Bank approved a kwacha-denominated Risk Sharing Credit Guarantee for its $100 million expansion programme, which the Bank expects to support more than 86,000 farmers, outgrowers and small businesses.

items.name: Supamoto (Emerging Cooking Solutions)
items.text: Sells clean cooking: fuel-efficient, IoT-enabled stoves with biomass pellets made from local waste at its plant in Ndola, on the Copperbelt, supplied with minimal upfront cost. In February 2025 PIDG and ElectriFI invested €4 million to finance 14,800 new stoves, for up to 74,000 people.

items.name: Impact Network
items.text: Runs the eSchool 360 model in rural Zambia: lessons by tablet and projector, teacher supervisors and weekly coaching for teachers, school supplies, rooftop solar power, locally hired teachers and parent-teacher associations. It piloted the model in eight schools in Katete District in 2013 and in 2017 set out to bring it to 35 more schools in the Eastern Province.

items.name: Zambia Industrial Commercial Bank (ZICB)
items.text: Lends to small and medium-sized enterprises in agriculture value chains. With EIB Global it is mobilising €30 million for agri-food businesses, at least 30% of it for businesses led or owned by women, backed by a €4 million risk-sharing facility.
